problem: Lead-acid car batteries drain when lights are left on, requiring jump starts, and are heavy.
business_model: Hardware: drop-in battery sold directly (target ~$200) via planned crowdfunding

founders.name: Hunter Scott
founders.background_notes: Hardware specialist with over 10 years designing electronics and building hardware teams per YC page.

competitors.name: Conventional lead-acid batteries
competitors.what: Group 35 lead-acid batteries, 40 lb, 3-4 year life, $120-$180

technical_complexity.rationale: Supercapacitor plus LiFePO4 hybrid with cut-off circuitry fitting a standard battery tray; TechCrunch notes only 10Ah reserve versus ~45Ah.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware design; no patents or moat reported in sources.

market_need_then: Jump-starts are a common roadside problem; TechCrunch (Aug 2015) said private beta had about a dozen units in the field.

brand_strength.rationale: Press coverage was about the product, not the brand; the name collides with later YC company Ohm (W23).

outcome_analysis: Ohm was a Summer 2015 drop-in supercapacitor car battery that got launch coverage in August 2015 and planned crowdfunding; the YC directory marks it Inactive, but no post-mortem, shutdown date or crowdfunding result was found, so the cause of failure is not public in the sources reached.
notes: Cause of shutdown not found. getohm.com returned 503. A search snippet said one directory shows last activity in 2020 (unverified). Directory status Inactive recorded as shutdown with no date. Web search budget for the session was exhausted before this shard started, so only direct page fetches were possible; outcome, funding cross-check, dated-competitor and branding searches could not be run.
